univsul_sulaymaniyah_2015_2019.publisher: Srwa Jalal Hama, University of Sulaimani, College of Humanities, Dept. of Geography; Sulaimani Journal for Human Sciences (p-ISSN 1813-0852, e-ISSN 2617-3034), journal pages 350-; received 29 Sep 2025, accepted 26 Nov 2025. Original data owners cited by the paper: Kurdistan Regional Government Ministry of Justice, Presidency of the Sulaymaniyah Court of Appeal (unpublished data 2015-2019); Sulaymaniyah Governorate Police Directorate, Statistics Section, murder crime statistics (unpublished); Sulaymaniyah Police Directorate, Anti-Crime Department and Murder Investigation Office (unpublished); population from KRG Sulaymaniyah Statistics Directorate estimates (unpublished).

univsul_sulaymaniyah_2015_2019.notes: Counts read from Table 1 (pdftotext -layout, Arabic right-to-left; checked: each district row sums to its printed 2015-2019 total and each year column sums to the printed governorate total 91, 106, 99, 113, 133; grand total 542). The percent column (share of 2015-2019 total) is kept as printed. Rates are from Table 2 exactly as printed; the paper computes them as crimes/population*100000. Several printed 2015 rates do not equal count/population from the same table (Said Sadiq 15.5 vs 11/86258; Dukan 16 vs 10/72679; Darbandikhan 5.4 vs 2/49905; Chamchamal 26 vs 29/168329); kept as printed, not corrected. The paper counts murder crimes (جرائم القتل) from police/court records, not victims. The 10 districts listed exclude Kalar, Rania and Pshdar (Garmiyan and Raparin administrations), so the governorate total row covers only these 10 districts. Not used: Table 3 (2019 by age group per district) - its wrapped layout could not be read reliably and its printed total row sums to 131, not the printed 133; Table 5 (per area) and Table 6 (causes, governorate only, court records). Boundary note: geoBoundaries ADM2 (OCHA 2021) uses older district lines; Qaradagh and Mawat (counted separately in the paper) appear to fall inside the geoBoundaries Al-Sulaymaniyah / Sharbazher polygons, and Sharazur and Said Sadiq inside the Halabcha polygon, so those four were left unmatched and the matched polygons for Al-Sulaymaniyah and Sharbazher may cover more ground than the paper's districts.

mahaweel_police_centres_2014_2019.publisher: Afrah Lafta Nayel and Raad Saeed Brebir; مجلة العلوم الإنسانية (Journal of Humanities), College of Education, issue 14 vol. 1, March 2023, hosted on the Iraqi Academic Scientific Journals platform (IASJ). Original data owner cited: Iraq Ministry of Interior, Babil Police Directorate / Al-Mahaweel Police Department, Criminal Statistics Division, unpublished data (2019-2020).
mahaweel_police_centres_2014_2019.notes: The PDF could not be saved: the shell fails the TLS handshake with iasj.rdd.edu.iq, so the tables were read twice through the WebFetch tool (raw Table 1 text in raw/mahaweel_table1_raw.txt). Checks: intentional murder per-year rows add to each centre total (43, 23, 34, 10) and the centres add to the printed district total 110; unintentional killing likewise (62, 21, 72, 9; total 164). Beating leading to death: reading Table 1 as count/percent pairs gives centre totals 40, 13, 30, 10, which add to the printed total 93 and match the printed percentages (43, 14, 32, 10); per-year rows are kept for Al-Mahaweel, Tunis and Al-Imam centres, where they add to those totals; the Al-Nil per-year rows add to 28, not 30, in the extracted text and were left out. Other columns (terrorism, kidnapping, suicide) not kept as they are not homicide. Police centres have no boundary file; only the district total is matched (geoBoundaries Al-Mahaweel). Not used: a Najaf governorate paper (University of Kufa, Journal of Geographical Research no. 32, murder by sub-district 2004-2014) whose text layer is too corrupted to read reliably.

problems: cosit.gov.iq reachable but no governorate-level homicide table found (searched site and web); only press releases and general publications. RETRY 17 Oct: cosit.gov.iq menu re-checked (no justice/crime section; only population, labour, living conditions, prices, national accounts, agriculture, industry, environment); Ministry of Health site (moh.gov.iq) returns 403 so cause-of-death by governorate could not be checked; krso.gov.krd returns 403 to the shell and searches found only press reports (Rudaw, Peregraf) quoting the KRG Interior Ministry; web.archive.org unreachable from the shell. A peer-reviewed paper on murders in Sulaymaniyah governorate 2015-2019 (Sulaimani Journal for Human Sciences, raw/univsul_paper.pdf, from https://sjh.univsul.edu.iq/SmartJournal_Uploads_sjh/1/articles/1440/15251227031823.pdf) uses unpublished police data obtained by the author; not used because it is not an official open publication. THIRD PASS 17 Oct: the Sulaymaniyah paper is now used under the research-paper route (district counts 2015-2019). Also tried: COSIT "Health indicators report 2024" (raw/cosit_health_indicators_2024.pdf) - suicide deaths by governorate (Table 19) but no homicide/assault deaths by governorate; cause-of-death table is national top-10 only. COSIT Annual Abstract 2024 chapter 10 (health and vital statistics) - registered deaths by governorate, all causes only. Kufa Journal of Nursing Sciences paper on injury deaths in Nineveh 2008-2012 (CC BY 4.0) gives governorate-wide totals only and its "violence" category covers the conflict years; not used. Also used: a paper on murder in Al-Mahaweel district (Babil) with police-centre counts 2014-2019 (see its source notes). Not used: a Najaf murder paper (2004-2014) with a corrupted text layer.
